v11.68 - u-104: istenen, çözülen ve gerçekten uygulanan artık aynı yüzeyde yan yana

Three different facts were being confused with each other, and the run detail
could show at most one of them at a time.

REQUESTED is what somebody chose — a member row, the mission, an agent's own
default, the fleet's. Visible in the composer and nowhere afterwards.

EFFECTIVE is what the ladder resolved that into and WHICH LAYER decided each
part. `runNote` said this in one line and is lossy by construction: it drops
every dimension whose origin is `cli`, drops `claude` because it is the default,
and never carried the workdir at all. So the commonest delegation of all — one
that took every default — was recorded as NOTHING, and the row that most needed
to say "nobody decided this" was the one that said least.

APPLIED is what the engine reports it actually served. It was on no surface and
in no op, so a model override that had been refused read exactly like one that
had been honoured.

WHAT IS KEPT. `step.ran` is the resolver's own answer, written beside `runNote`
at the spawn — every dimension with its origin, `cli` included. `runNote` is
untouched: a caller reading it is unaffected, and steps recorded before this say
so rather than drawing five empty rows.

WHAT IS READ BACK. `appliedDimensions()` takes the models the transcript records
and the permission mode the CLI wrote. ‼️ Silence is a VALUE: a field the
transcript does not state comes back null and every surface prints "not
reported" rather than echoing the request, because that echo is exactly how a
mismatch hides. Effort is reported by no engine today and says so.

THE SURFACE. One renderer, one vocabulary, five dimensions in a fixed order,
used by every participant on the page. The ROW carries a mark (SHORTHAND) — ⚙
some layer decided something, ≠ the engine came back with something else,
nothing at all when everything fell to the CLI — and the panel carries the table
(AFTip, opening with the current effective line: MIRROR).

‼️ AN ALIAS IS NOT A SUBSTITUTION. Every CLI takes a short name and writes the
full id into its transcript — `opus` served by `claude-opus-5`, `grok-code` by
`grok-code-fast-1`. Compared as strings that is a disagreement on almost every
row, and a warning that fires on almost every row is one nobody reads. Caught in
the render: the first picture had ≠ on the orchestrator and on every worker.

THE HEADER, IN TWO SUBJECTS. One muted line used to hold the lead, the planner's
model, the whole team, the workdir and the approval mode — and its member chips
repeated the DECLARED values while the rows below showed the RESOLVED ones, so
the same subject was drawn twice, differently. Now: Orchestrator (lead, its
profile, its transcript) and Workers (each member, with what was declared on its
row, what the ladder resolved, and what the engine applied). ONE SUBJECT — the
Workers panel names the ROUND a reading came from, never the step's own title,
which belongs to the row.

‼️ And the orchestrator's non-choices are said as non-choices. Its engine is
Claude Code always, it has no permission mode at all (its write and spawn tools
are cut off by name), and it runs in the LEAD AGENT'S folder rather than the
mission workdir. Printing "nobody set it — the CLI decided" for those would be a
lie about a control that does not exist, so they carry a sixth origin word,
`fixed`, which is the only one that is not a layer — and which earns no ⚙,
because a glyph every run wears says nothing.

BRIDGE. missions.status keeps `ran` exactly as it was and adds `dimensions` (the
same answer whole) and `applied`, per step and for the planner. The index is
walked once per call, not once per step.
